title: Fixed Deep Shafts and Sloping Gallery Cutaway
description: One newly authored complete dry subterranean-gallery architectural half-section. A continuous solid earth-and-lining appearance contains a low through-gallery falling gently toward its open end and two separate deep vertical access shafts that genuinely join that gallery. The outer grade slopes independently in height through the same section; the two shafts therefore reach different depths. The entire front half is deliberately removed as a fixed explanatory section, exposing the real shaft-to-gallery intersections, full gallery floor, rear wall and retained roof intervals. A single shared-vertex closed material boundary forms the whole terrain/void section with no overlapping block faces. Unlike the old shallow stone road culvert, the main relation is deep surface access into one continuous lower passage rather than a transverse channel under a road cap. Unlike the mine access bay, this actually contains below-grade shaft depths and their connecting gallery, without machinery, rails or a surface assembly of separate old props. All coordinates newly authored. Three opaque solid PBR roles, metres Z up, full horizontal bounds centred and lowest base Z0. One architectural module zero scenes. Abstract dry waterwork-inspired artistic cutaway, not a reconstruction of a named site or a civil-engineering design. The half-section does not claim a fully enclosed tunnel; its missing front half is intentional. No water, groundwater collection, hydraulic grade, flow, excavation, ventilation, accessible route, soil stability, load, construction, historical precision or engineering safety capability.
